title: Generic geometry of an ordinary blowup of a reduced scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a reduced scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Q$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $J\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be a coherent quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent]. Suppose $U=S\setminus V(J)$ is dense in every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components]. For the ordinary blowup $b:W=\operatorname{Bl}_J(S)\to S$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], $W$ is reduced, locally Noetherian with finitely many irreducible components [pqf-def-locnoeth], and of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, and $b$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The restriction $b^{-1}U\to U$ is an isomorphism and $b^{-1}U$ is dense in every irreducible component of $W$. The map $b$ induces a bijection of generic points [def-sc-generic-point], with isomorphic residue fields, between the irreducible components of $W$ and those of $S$. Equivalently, corresponding reduced components are birational, meaning isomorphic on dense open subschemes. The empty scheme and the unit ideal are allowed.

proof.text: Coherence of $J$ implies finite type by [pqf-def-coherent]. Apply [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper] to obtain properness of $b$. In particular $b$ is of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Composing with $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$ using [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] gives that $W$ is of finite type over $\mathbf Q$. The spectrum of $\mathbf Q$ is locally Noetherian: its ring is a field, whose only ideals are zero and the unit ideal. Thus [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] applies to both $S$ and $W$, giving local Noetherianity. Both have finite affine covers by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; refine these by Noetherian affine neighbourhoods and take a finite subcover using quasi-compactness. Each member has Noetherian underlying space by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]. A descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes on each member, hence globally after the maximum of finitely many stabilization indices. Thus both underlying spaces are Noetherian and have finitely many components by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components]. Every subset of either space is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets]; in particular the open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow S$ is quasi-compact (apply this to its intersection with each affine open). It is quasi-separated since its diagonal is an isomorphism.

Since components cover $S$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], the hypothesis on every component implies that $U$ is dense in $S$. At every point of $U=S\setminus V(J)$ the stalk of $J$ is the unit ideal, so $J|_U=\mathcal O_U$. By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], $V=b^{-1}U\to U$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic] to the reduced scheme $S$ and the quasi-compact, quasi-separated dense open immersion $j$ verified in Step 1. Its scheme-theoretic image is $S$. Since $j$ is quasi-compact, [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] identifies its image ideal with the actual kernel of $\mathcal O_S\to j_*\mathcal O_U$; this kernel is therefore zero. Thus $j$ is scheme-theoretically dense in the precise injectivity sense of [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open].

Apply [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-preserves-density] to $j$ and $J$: quasi-compactness, schematic density, finite type of $J$, and $J|_U=\mathcal O_U$ have all been checked. It gives injectivity of $\mathcal O_W\to k_*\mathcal O_V$, where $k:V\hookrightarrow W$, by [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open]. The open $V$ is quasi-compact by Step 1. This also implies topological density: a nonempty open $T\subset W$ disjoint from $V$ would force $\mathcal O_W|_T$ to inject into the zero sheaf, impossible at a point of $T$ since its local ring has a proper maximal ideal.

source.place: Tag 02OS (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor); the schematic-density argument from its effective Cartier exceptional divisor

proof.text: The open $U$ is reduced: its local rings are the corresponding local rings of $S$. Thus $V\cong U$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. For any open $T\subseteq W$, let $s\in\mathcal O_W(T)$ satisfy $s^n=0$ with $n\ge1$. Its restriction to $T\cap V$ is nilpotent and hence zero. The injectivity in Step 3 forces $s=0$. Every ring of sections of $W$ is therefore reduced, which is the equivalent criterion in [def-pc-reduced-scheme].

source.place: Tag 056E (lemma-reduced-subscheme-closure), proof by restricting nilpotent sections to the schematically dense reduced open

proof.text: Here is the finite-component argument in full. In either $X=S$ or $X=W$, let $C$ be a component and remove the union of all other components. This is an open subset of $X$, nonempty because a maximal irreducible subset cannot be covered by finitely many other closed components. A dense open $O$ meets this open, so $C\cap O$ is nonempty; it is an open subset of the irreducible space $C$, hence dense and irreducible. Its closure in $X$ is $C$. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], components cover $X$, and every irreducible subset of $O$ has irreducible closure contained in a component of $X$; maximality now shows that the components of $O$ are exactly the distinct $C\cap O$. Apply this with $O=U$ and $O=V$, dense by hypothesis and Step 3. The isomorphism $V\cong U$ matches these components, and taking closures gives a bijection between the components of $W$ and $S$. In particular $V$ is dense in every component of $W$. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober] each component has a unique generic point. This point belongs to any nonempty open subset of the component (otherwise its whole closure would be in the closed complement). Thus all these generic points lie in $V$ or $U$, and the isomorphism matches them. The component bijection is the map induced by $b$: continuity gives $b(\overline{\{\xi\}})\subseteq\overline{\{b(\xi)\}}$.

source.place: Tag 0BFM (lemma-blow-up-and-irreducible-components); finite-component topological argument using the dense open of Steps 2--3

proof.text: At corresponding generic points $\xi\in V$ and $\eta=b(\xi)\in U$, the map of local rings induced by $b$ is an isomorphism because $V\to U$ is an isomorphism and open restriction does not change local rings. Quotienting by the maximal ideals gives the asserted isomorphism $\kappa(\eta)\to\kappa(\xi)$ by [def-weil-residue-field]. For corresponding components $C'\subset W$, $C\subset S$, the isomorphism $V\to U$ identifies $C'\cap V$ with $C\cap U$. Equip components with their reduced induced structures. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], applied inside the two isomorphic opens, shows that this is an isomorphism of the reduced component opens. They are dense by Step 5, proving the stated birationality.

Properness makes the image $b(W)$ closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism] (take the identity base change). It contains $U$ by Step 2. Since $U$ is dense in $S$, this closed image is all of $S$, which is surjectivity by [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. If $S$ is empty the finite covers, components and generic-point sets above are empty and surjectivity is vacuous. If $J=\mathcal O_S$, then $U=S$ and Step 2 identifies the whole blowup with $S$; all assertions follow as well.
